security_spec.violation_condition: In FreeBSD's RISC-V port, if Smip fast-interrupt context save/restore (via mnxti/mscratchcsw) is implemented without also implementing the double-trap extension (Ssdtcp/Smdbltrp), any synchronous exception (page fault, TLB miss) occurring during the hardware-injected register save/restore sequence produces unrecoverable trap state: mnepc/xepc holds the *first* trap's PC rather than the faulting instruction's PC, the kernel cannot distinguish the nested-trap scenario, and returning to the first trap's PC immediately re-traps without forward progress.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: mnxti|mscratchcsw|CSR_MNXTI|CSR_MSCRATCHCSW without Ssdtcp|Smdbltrp|double.?trap check in ISA extension probing or init code
security_spec.summary: Smip fault handling requires double-trap extensions for recoverability; FreeBSD neither implements Smip nor probes for Ssdtcp/Smdbltrp in identcpu.c, so any future CLIC enablement without first adding double-trap recovery would make synchronous exceptions during fast-interrupt save/restore permanently unrecoverable (unbounded re-trap loop)

findings.finding: parse_ext_s() recognizes only 5 S-mode extensions (sstc, svnapot, svpbmt, svinval, sscofpmf). Neither Smip (fast-interrupt) nor Smdbltrp/Ssdbltrp/Ssdtcp (double-trap) appear in the recognized-extension list. Since FreeBSD does not implement mnxti/mscratchcsw fast-interrupt save/restore at all, the vulnerability precondition ('Smip implemented without double-trap') cannot be satisfied. The kernel has no hardware-injected register save/restore sequence that could produce unrecoverable nested-trap state.

No mnepc/mnstatus/mncause/mnscratch CSR definitions exist in the kernel. No CSR_MNXTI (0x345) or CSR_MSCRATCHCSW (0x348/0x349) definitions. The SiFive CLIC fast-interrupt CSR space is entirely absent from FreeBSD's RISC-V register map. Without these register definitions, no kernel code path can invoke hardware-injected save/restore sequences, so the double-trap-on-fast-interrupt vulnerability cannot arise.
findings.snippet: (No mnxti/mscratchcsw CSR definitions found anywhere in sys/riscv/)

findings.finding: cpu_desc.smode_extensions bitmask has only 5 defined flags (SV_SSTC through SV_SSCOFPMF at bits 0-4). No SV_SMIP, SV_SMDBLTRP, SV_SSDTCP, or SV_SSDBLTRP flags. The kernel's feature-probing infrastructure has no slot to record Smip or double-trap capability, consistent with the fact that neither feature is implemented. This is structurally correct: no false capability-claim is made.

S-mode extension print formatting knows only the same 5 extensions. No Smip/mnxti/mscratchcsw or Smdbltrp/Ssdbltrp/Ssdtcp bits are advertised. Userspace and kernel logs correctly reflect that FreeBSD does not expose fast-interrupt or double-trap features.

encoding.h defines standard RISC-V CSRs (sstatus, sie, stvec, sscratch, sepc, scause, stval, satp, etc.) but zero CSRs from the Smip fast-interrupt extension (mnxti at 0x345, mscratchcsw at 0x348/0x349, mnepc, mnstatus, mncause, mnscratch) or Smdbltrp/Ssdtcp double-trap CSRs. This absence is consistent and correct given neither feature is used.

Kernel-wide grep for 'mnxti', 'mscratchcsw', 'CSR_MNXTI', 'CSR_MSCRATCHCSW', 'Smip', 'Smaia', 'Ssaia', 'Ssdtcp', 'Smdbltrp', 'Smstateen', 'Smrnmi' returns zero matches in sys/riscv/. FreeBSD's RISC-V port is entirely free of Smip fast-interrupt implementation. The vulnerability pattern 'mnxti|mscratchcsw without double-trap check' is a vacuous condition — there is no fast-interrupt code to check. The security spec's violation condition is not triggered.
findings.snippet: (Zero matches across all of sys/riscv/ for Smip/double-trap related symbols)
